content:
After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to all users, bringing Apple's all-new Siri AI, refined Liquid Glass changes, major new Safari features, and a slew of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here's everything new.

At this year's WWDC, Apple introduced its operating systems in a slightly different way than users and developers are used to.

Instead of going platform by platform with new features and devoting little time to each OS, Apple spent most of its time on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of the new features rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

Nevertheless, macOS 27 Golden Gate adds a number of welcome improvements in both design and functionality, starting with some long-awaited Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and interface improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's new design language, it was visually a bit lackluster compared to the other systems, particularly iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has spent more time further integrating the new Liquid Glass into the system while bringing some of the visual adjustments from iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 to macOS. These include a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users adjust the level of transparency or opacity.

There's also a fun Easter egg hiding in the Liquid Glass display settings, which features Clarus the Dogcow — keep scrolling past the bottom of the demo panel to find it.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also gets fresh app icons to match the Liquid Glass aesthetic, with more layering in light, dark, tinted, and clear system appearances to add depth and detail.

The red, yellow, and green buttons that Apple introduced mid-beta have been redesigned. Rather than the previous flat green, yellow, and red design, they now feature a Liquid Glass look, complete with a lively bounce effect when clicked (or perhaps tapped soon?) and dragged and released.

Another thoughtful interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to unify the corner radius of system windows and apps, no longer dynamically changing it based on UI elements in the window's menu bar.

While Apple's intention was deliberate, many assumed the inconsistent corner radius was a bug, so Apple specifically called out this change during its WWDC keynote.

Similarly controversial, and shelved in macOS 27 Golden Gate, was the number of icons next to menu items. In macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple added symbols next to nearly every command in its apps, intending to make menus easier to scan at a glance, but the result was criticized as making menus busier and sometimes harder to quickly skim.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple (thankfully) reversed course and removed most of these icons, returning menus to a cleaner, more visually streamlined appearance.

Other visual refinements in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and a more prominent indication of the active window — both of which were equally controversial in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This is arguably the most important new feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple's reimagined Siri is developed in partnership with Google Gemini models and is deeply integrated into the system, complete with a standalone app.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device indexing system for user data and lives in both Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The Siri app looks and largely functions similarly to other AI assistant apps users are accustomed to: a sidebar on the left lists the user's conversations across all compatible platforms, while the main chat panel lets users enter prompts, attach images or files, or begin a conversation with their voice. The app also supports searching and pinning conversations, which is a plus for users with different workflows.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and the user's context to provide useful and specific answers. During beta testing, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive reviews, though it can sometimes be a bit slower to respond than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants.

Another useful feature of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with both native and third-party apps and perform actions directly, dramatically advancing Siri's app integration from before.

Importantly, developers need to expose their apps' content and functionality through the App Intents framework, so the assistant's relevant performance will continue to improve as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Finally, there's a system-wide "Ask Siri" option available from the right-click context menu for selected text, images, or files, allowing users to ask Siri directly. For example, users can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri to learn more about it, or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite, proofread, adjust the tone, or provide feedback on the writing.

Siri AI launches with support for English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support coming in October. Currently, Siri AI is not available in China or the EU due to regulatory issues.

Apple Intelligence

We've covered Apple's new foundation models in detail, but in short, Apple developed new versions of its Apple Intelligence models for its 2027 operating systems. Here's how Apple describes each model:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3 billion parameter dense model, delivering higher quality. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model. It natively supports multimodality, enabling richer expressive voice and more accurate dictation. This 20 billion parameter model is built on Apple's cutting-edge research and uses a sparse architecture that activates 1 to 4 billion parameters on demand. AFM 3 Core Advanced is unlocked and optimized by our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse, optimized for speed, efficiency, and performance. ADM 3 Cloud (Image), used for image generation and editing, unlocking more advanced photo editing tools, the new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most powerful server-side model, powering the most demanding use cases such as agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two local models: AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced, with the others running in the cloud. The performance of these two local models depends on the Mac's hardware — specifically, the memory available for running dynamic parameters and other AI workloads.

As for how Apple Intelligence is implemented in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it's a mixed bag. The models themselves perform quite well for everyday tasks, such as helping draft emails, proofreading documents, or summarizing text.

The problem is that Apple is currently somewhat overzealous in how and when it surfaces Siri AI, which can at times feel overwhelming to users and even get in the way of what they were trying to do.

One nice new Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the addition of a Visual Intelligence shortcut. Holding Command-Shift-Space lets users select any area of the screen to immediately ask Siri about it. This works with images, PDFs, text, or anything displayed on screen.

Unfortunately, not every Mac compatible with macOS 27 will run the new Apple Intelligence — it requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here are the Macs Apple officially lists as supporting the new features:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later)
  • Mac mini with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 or later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple Silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support the languages currently supported by existing versions of Apple Intelligence, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Due to regulatory issues, Apple Intelligence is currently not available in China. Apple also notes that some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features will have usage limits, though the company has not publicly disclosed specifics.

Performance and stability improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted a multitude of improvements that would apply across all operating systems.

For macOS 27 Golden Gate, that means faster AirDrop transfers, smoother network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (particularly for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with support for selective priority syncing.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves Safari and Calendar scrolling performance, as well as Mission Control and Spaces animations. Apple has also tweaked Mail indexing and search, along with the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other refinements include more consistent and persistent window positions on external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, support for more high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes on external displays, and improved touch support in Sidecar — including tap gestures, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and Markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces Notify Me, a new Safari feature that can monitor web pages and alert users when relevant changes occur, such as price drops, restocks, event registration openings, or nearly anything else users ask it to track.

Notify Me can be set to check hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, with the option to specify days of the week and times.

Additionally, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces "Describe an Extension," allowing users to create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples spanning productivity, focus, creativity, design, and development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both of these features are accessible from the "More Options" hamburger menu on the right side of the current Safari tab.

For users who frequently find themselves with dozens of tabs open, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs based on topic.

Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate also gets a fun new feature: a pull-to-refresh gesture, just like in iOS and iPadOS, where users can swipe down past the rubber-band effect to reload the page.

This gesture is also available in other system apps like Mail, News, and Calendar, which many see as further foreshadowing the rumored touchscreen Mac that could be announced this year.

iPhone Mirroring

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios, which many see as an early signal that Apple is preparing for a foldable iPhone.

With the iPhone Duo now officially available, Mac users can get an early taste of that experience. Unfortunately, Apple has noted that iPhone Mirroring still isn't available in the EU.

Shortcuts

This might be one of the most practically valuable Apple Intelligence additions across this year's Apple OS updates.

While Shortcuts itself is already a fairly approachable automation tool, it can still be daunting for everyday users. Now users can simply describe what they want to do, and Apple Intelligence will turn it into a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app offers several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate to Spanish
  • Write a haiku about the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist when I arrive at the gym
  • Make a recipe with these leftover ingredients
  • Summarize my day every morning
  • Prioritize my to-do list every morning
  • Get directions when I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when Bedtime begins
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when I open the TV app

By the way, if you want to dive deeper into Shortcuts, be sure to check out Stephen Robles' excellent content on YouTube and Instagram. You can also check out MacStories' Shortcuts Playground, an even more powerful natural language shortcut creation tool.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three editing tools powered by Apple Intelligence: an enhanced Clean Up that can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from photos; Extend, which can generate surrounding areas of an image if users feel the original photo was cropped too tightly; and Spatial Reframing, which can change the angle and composition of a photo after it's been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing, allowing Windows and Android users to join via iCloud.com.

Other new features include the ability to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transition effects, and playback duration, a new star rating system, and a new "Shot by Me" album.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate details

  • Calendar can be used to add, edit, or update events by description.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names for files and folders based on their contents.
  • Image Playground has expanded support for different styles and uses new foundation models for better generation results.
  • Maps' Flyover experience has been enhanced, bringing better textures, richer detail, and sharper rendering to hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages has finally integrated tapback notifications and improved cross-device syncing.
  • *Notes supports handwritten notes and sketches written with a trackpad, expands Markdown copy-and-paste support, and adds Section Links.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts and picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate is also the final version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, "only apps will stop running after being updated on a Mac with Apple Silicon" — you can read more about that here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official information, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Macs:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

What's your favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.

Notable Amazon products

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirTag (2nd generation) — 4-pack
  • MacBook Neo
